reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) requested breaking down the large patch into smaller, reviewable pieces and removing special-case tests that are hard to maintain.
reviews.raw_body:
In any case, we have to break this down into reviewable pieces. We neglected
selftests for too long.

... and there are some schlopped tests in there that we really shouldn't have as
they are way too special and hard to maintain.

Like this monstrosity:

+/*
+ * A folio faulted on another CPU can remain in that CPU's pending LRU batch.
+ * MADV_COLD drains only the calling CPU and must safely skip the non-LRU
+ * folio without changing the mapping.
+ */
+static void test_madvise_cold_remote_lru_batch(void)
+{

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that some tests can be deleted without losing fidelity, agrees to show the work, and suggests removing ~15-20 tests.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah the intent of these particular tests was to ensure I capture ever
weird branch in the code before i went refactoring it so I ensured there
was no loss of fidelity.

I think we can reasonably delete ~15-20 of these tests.  That said, the
code itself is not schlopp, but I believe in showing the work.

~Gregory

2026-09-24.patch_summary: This patch adds self-tests to exercise the MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT functionality in the Linux kernel. The tests cover both user-visible contracts, such as verifying that MADV_COLD does not populate PTE holes and that PAGEOUT preserves unevictable base pages, as well as implementation details like folio and page-table behavior under various scenarios. The patch includes 28 cases to test these behaviors, with some tests intentionally asserting specific conditions to detect unintended changes during a planned refactor of the page-table walker.
